name: driverkit-workspace
//workspaces: Declared for npm as well as pnpm-workspace.yaml, and not as a second opinion:
it is what creates node_modules/driverkit as a link to packages/driverkit.
That link is how a bare `driverkit` or `driverkit/widget` import resolves at
all -- there is no `paths` mapping, deliberately, so the tests and the demo
resolve the same way a consumer does: through the package's own `exports`,
including the `node` condition that keeps the relay off a page. pnpm does the
same thing from its own file; both are listed so neither manager is special.

//test: The build runs first. Nothing in the suite imports `dist/` directly -- every
test reaches into `../src/*.ts` by relative path -- but `test/packaging.test.ts`
asks what the package publishes, and that question needs the built files on
disk. It skips itself when they are absent rather than passing vacuously, and
a skipped packaging test is how a packaging regression would get through.
//e2e: The demo in a real browser: the one thing the unit suite cannot do, since
every visual claim in them is asserted against `test/fake-dom.ts`. Needs a
browser on disk -- `npx playwright install chromium`, or DK_CHANNEL=chrome to
use the Chrome you already have. See e2e/README.md. Not part of `npm test`:
it starts a server and a browser, and `npm test` must stay a pure function of
